query: What should I focus on in this table to identify actions that could improve product scores?

per_column.name: helpfulness_ratio
per_column.rationale: Fraction of readers finding a review helpful. This is a property of the review's reception, not a candidate cause of the product score nor a common cause of a treatment and the score. It does not fit a treatment or confounder role for improving product scores.

per_column.name: review_length
per_column.rationale: Mechanical text-length feature. Not a plausible common cause of both an action (treatment) and the product score; at best a generic covariate, not a genuine confounder.

per_column.name: mentions_quality_issues
per_column.rationale: Whether the review flags quality problems. As an 'action to improve scores' framing, product quality is a candidate cause whose effect on score is being attributed. Functions as a treatment-like feature, though it is really a reflection of the outcome (potential collider/reverse-causation concern).

per_column.name: mentions_value_price
per_column.rationale: Flags price/value mentions; pricing is a plausible actionable cause of the score, so it reads as a candidate treatment. Not a common cause of another treatment and the outcome, so not a confounder.

per_column.name: mentions_delivery
per_column.rationale: Flags delivery mentions; delivery experience is an actionable candidate cause of the score, so treatment-like. Not a confounder.

per_column.name: low_score_with_issue
per_column.rationale: Interaction defined jointly from low score (the outcome) and issue mention. Conditioning on a variable that is a function of the outcome induces collider/selection bias; labelling it a driver would be an error.

per_column.name: high_satisfaction_indicator
per_column.rationale: A satisfaction/high-score indicator is essentially a restatement of the outcome, not a cause or confounder of it.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply several candidate treatments (quality, price, delivery mentions) framed as actionable causes of the product score, so requirement (a) is partially met. However, requirement (b) is not satisfied: there are NO variables that plausibly cause BOTH one of these treatments AND the outcome and would need adjustment. The remaining columns are mechanical (review_length, helpfulness_ratio), restatements of the outcome (high_satisfaction_indicator), or an outcome-derived interaction that is a collider (low_score_with_issue). No genuine, data-surfaced confounder is present, so the causal-attribution claim fails: the schema sets up naive treatment-outcome associations without any confounding control.
